📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Take-Two CEO Ben Feder says that GTA 6 is "the last pre-AI blockbuster video game of its kind" and will mark the end of an era in game development.

In a recent development, in an article for Fortune, Feder indicates "the moment will be cultural, the experience epic, and the game, I expect, a masterpiece. It will also be the last of its kind." But this is not down to Rockstar's quality control dwindling, or AI making game development faster and cheaper, but rather that GTA 6 "represents the culmination of a model of creativity that AI is about to upend.".

He notes that a change of direction or abandoning an idea for a game can cost both in time and technology, and that "AI lowers the cost of changing your mind.".

Sources indicate that feder likens the arrival of AI to photography arriving in a world of painting. "When photography arrived, many visual artists feared for their livelihoods, and some were right: the market for commissioned likenesses collapsed." He adds, "others asked a different question: What will we create now? Freed from the need to represent reality faithfully, they created newly introduced, even radical, art forms: Impressionism, Cubism and abstraction.".

"I suspect cultural historians will one day look back on GTA 6 the way art historians look back on the last great realist painters," he adds, calling it "the fullest expression of one creative model just before the boundaries of the medium broke open to reveal entirely new forms.".

Sources indicate that of course, it's worth noting that Feder is currently a managing partner at TIRTA Ventures, which is described as "an early-stage AI fund investing at the frontier of digital experiences, creativity, and platform ecosystems," which likely has an impact on his feelings on the inevitably of AI in games. But it is somewhat true that as the slop becomes harder to filter out of game development, those fully dedicated to human-made art will be at the forefront of new forms of expression.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game.
  • In a recent development, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more!
  • Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest.

It has been revealed that I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

In a recent development, conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past.".

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

It has been revealed that overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

Recent findings suggest that first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new patch continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

Industry observers note that the big inciting incident of this newly introduced chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent newly introduced characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Recent findings suggest that version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this patch, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

It has been revealed that as part of the same upgrade, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Sources indicate that currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 upgrade, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, you’ll find upcoming items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 releases and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

After days of controversy, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.
  • After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has announced Huang's resignation as firm president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately.
  • In a recent development, "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as leader of one of the most valuable companies in the world.

After days mired in controversy, which began amid reports of Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, Nvidia has announced Huang's resignation as firm president, chief executive officer, and board member, effective immediately. Finance chief Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO and will remain in the position until a permanent CEO is chosen.

In a recent development, "Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors wrote in a statement accompanying the news. "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the tech giant's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.".

Kress, in the same announcement, claims she intends to build on the foundation laid by Huang over the past 33 years, and "continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's no mention of gaming graphics cards in there.

Nvidia's announcement ends by thanking Huang for his time at the tech giant: "Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.".

In a recent development, nvidia's board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang amid allegations he had participated in a second affair, this time with a subordinate, following reports of his alleged affair with a Chinese spy. That initial incident prompted a company-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation exploring whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Nvidia will likely remain under increased scrutiny moving forward. There are particular concerns around the company's chips being imported to China despite trade bans.

Gears of War: E-Day appears to be something of a console mover, and I'd wager help from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 played a part too. Microsoft has claimed the top two spots in Circana's projected best-selling video games chart for October 2026, taking both physical and digital dollar sales into consideration.

Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October, which Piscatella also noted makes it the "19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty franchise release has been the best-selling game of its debut month".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.
  • It has been revealed that earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam.
  • It has been revealed that new turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More indie developers say they've been forced to delay the impending release of their games as a result of Steam's growing approvals backlog - a relatively recent problem that's believed to stem from an influx of AI slop on the platform.

It has been revealed that earlier this month, developers began complaining about delays to Valve's approval process, which was extending the time it took to get their games published on Steam. Valve responded, explaining approval times could now take up to 12 days, due to the number of submissions it was having to re-review. One week on, the situation doesn't seem to have improved.

It has been revealed that new turn-based tower defence game Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, co-developed by acclaimed indie designer Rami Ismail and Aesthetician Labs, was previously set for release on 10th November. Unfortunately, the game has now been delayed while the wait continues for Valve to review the latest build.

"We're still waiting for Steam to give us the final greenlight and finish their build review process," publisher Mystic Forge wrote on the Steam forums. "We have been stuck waiting for it for a few weeks now and unfortunately we just don't know when they will get around to reviewing it at this point.".

Speaking to Eurogamer, Ismail added that Australia Did It has been in Steam's approval queue for much longer than he's used to: "We've been in the queue since 20th October, failed over a minor controller input issue on 5th November (which we resolved the same day), and we've been waiting again since with no meaningful response from Valve despite follow-ups.".

"I'm used to hold-and-wait patterns on console," Ismail continued, "but Steam has historically been much more snappy - 10-14 days pre-launch was usually enough to fail twice and still ship on time," he added.

According to recent reports, amazing Slot Survivor (A.S.S.), the debut title from TwoMenGames, is facing similar concerns, and has had to retract its release date announcement after being stuck in Steam's approval queue. Amazing Slot Survivor, which adds a slot machine spin to the bullet heaven auto-shooting genre, was initially set for release on 13th November.

"Steam's review process for the release is taking longer than we expected," TwoMenGames wrote in a message on Steam. "We know many of you have been counting on the schedule we declared earlier, and we are very sorry to bring you this [postponement] news instead of the good news you were hoping for." Amazing Slot Survivor's demo, which was previously set to disappear with the game's full release, has returned to Steam until the developer announces a new launch date.

These are far from the only examples, and a cursory look on social media reveals many more indie games are affected by the problem, including the likes of Bottled by Bears, and Food Devils.

Valve recently attempted to address the delays its facing by introducing stricter submission guidelines designed to stop the lowest-effort games, such as those vibe-coded entirely with gen-AI, from joining its approval queue. However, Ismail doesn't think that's good enough.

Sources indicate that "I am concerned that Valve trying to avoid taking a political position on AI is forcing them into choices that will inevitably be worse for developers," he told Eurogamer. "If sloppers can submit several game clones a day through automated systems, the only way for Valve to stem the tide of games damaging genuine developers' work is to put constraints on game distribution, increase fees, or make the process more complicated.

"In the 'open market' Valve seems to so adore, they're going to be the ones carrying the costs for moderation, so I don't think they'll like the open market on this - but there's no outcome of this that allows Valve neutrality on AI and not do things that will ultimately make life worse for genuine developers," he added.

Animal Crossing: Fresh Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The revision, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

Their contributions were then double-confirmed by the full GTA 6 credits, which Rockstar published once launch time hit.

I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

"I’m the host of GTA 6’s 'non-stop ‘80s' radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well!" Yankovic remarked. "As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!".

Somewhere out there, Weird Al is securing the love of his virtual latina wife, and I think that's beautiful.

It has been revealed that yankovic is just one of countless recognizable names you'll find if you scroll down the GTA 6 credits. Among the core cast, SNL alumnus Bobby Moynihan voices Cal, Jason's bumbling, conspiracy-brained buddy. The pair's criminal boss man, Brian Heder, is performed by legendary Stephen Root—who you'll likely recognize as Bill Dauterive on King of the Hill, Milton in Office Space, and all kinds of magnificent weirdos across the Coen brothers filmography.

But it's the radio talent where GTA 6's credits get particularly wild. It's a cavalcade of international music icons, comedians, and film figures. While driving around GTA 6, you might hear Lana Del Rey hosting Back Country Radio, or Latin music phenom Bad Bunny on Cocoteo FM. On Dirty South Classics, there's Trina, Trick Daddy, and Gucci Mane. Pop station Flash FM is helmed by Robyn and Alex Consani—the first transgender model to win Model of the Year at the British Fashion Awards and celebrated TikTok goofball. Keith Richards is in there. I didn't even know he was still capable of speech.

On talk radio, you can hear Ted Lasso's Jason Sudeikis, Abbot Elementary's Janelle James, and John Leguizamo of being John Leguizamo fame. Stavros Halkias is on there doing a Conservative talk radio bit. But maybe the most compelling inclusion, for me, is that Kaleidoscope FM is hosted by Jeremy Irons. The Academy Award-winning actor. You were in Kafka, Jeremy. How'd you end up in cyber-Florida?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with.

Sources indicate that is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

Industry observers note that the latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's notable because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Industry observers note that beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

According to recent reports, perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

📅 16 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (445 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Metro series is finally, officially back with a fresh installment.
  • According to recent reports, 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however.
  • Sources indicate that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Metro series is finally, officially back with a fresh installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

According to recent reports, 2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

Sources indicate that what won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The fresh protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Industry observers note that today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch.
  • Recent findings suggest that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D.
  • World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.

Recent findings suggest that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

World of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

However, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!

Reddit user Playful_Artichoke981 has been at the forefront of requests asking Blizzard to address the problem , though they're far from alone. Currently, Oceania players see full daylight in-game from around midnight to 6am in the morning, which obviously is far from normal gaming hours for the majority of players in the region.

In a recent development, "We don't hate the nighttime. We just want variety," writes Playful_Artichoke981. "We don't want to have to compromise our sleep schedules to experience this game in all its glory." Another user, cuddlegoop, echoes the sentiment: "I am totally fine with my day/night changing when I join an NA party. Just let me see the sun! I was up late last night and the view over the bay at Shadowfan Keep in the dawn was so beautiful I want to see stuff like that more often.".

Eurogamer has contacted Blizzard to ask if it has plans to address the issue, but we've not received a response at the time of writing.

World of Warcraft: Forever is proving exceptionally popular, breaking records as the biggest launch in the series' history. And based on what I've played this week, it's looking to be a brilliant MMO that's well worth jumping into, if you have the time.

VisionQuest showrunner Terry Matalas has confirmed Jim Hammond fought in World War 2, alongside Steve Rogers' Captain America.

Jim Hammond finally made his MCU debut in the Disney Plus show, though his costume could first be glimpsed in Captain America: The First Avenger, way back in 2011. He was created by Phineas Horton.

"I think he was doing exactly that," Matalas shared in an interview, when asked if Hammond fought Nazis or saved people in London. "I think he was part of the Invaders. In the comic books, he kills Hitler. The idea is there is a whole series that happened that we didn't see that's about that father and son, and the gang in World War 2.".

When the interviewer asked if, during The First Avenger, Steve Rogers was also part of the Invaders and had a side mission, Matalas confirmed: "You would see Jim Hammond." Check it out below.

Terry Matalas notes that he envisioned Jim Hammond to have been on the Invaders and fought alongside Steve Rogers in WWII‼️ Let him make a special presentation where Jim kills Hitler NOW https://t.co/J586M2qezlNovember 19, 2026.

In Marvel comics, the Invaders was a team of superheroes that fought in World War 2, which included Steve Rogers, Bucky Barnes, Namor the Sub-Mariner, Jim Hammond, and his sidekick Toro.

However, the movies steered clear of this team – likely due to rights concerns – and instead we saw Steve Rogers and Bucky Barnes allied with the Howling Commandos. Still, thanks to Matalas, we can now imagine the Invaders were involved in the war, just off-screen.

VisionQuest also resurrected Wanda Maximoff in a shock post-credits scene directly setting up Avengers: Doomsday. What's next for the Maximoff family is anyone's guess.

It has been revealed that next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the upcoming content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Patch kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

Recent findings suggest that more interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the fresh season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is presently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

Recent findings suggest that I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite swiftly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Sources indicate that different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create newly introduced effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer.
  • It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 certainly does that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 (well, some of us) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already.

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC.

Sources indicate that maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my console unable to keep up with me. I'll tell you how I'm getting on in another fifty hours. Cool, see you in three days, then?

In a recent development, I was dreading playing GTA 6 on my OG PS5—a dusty ornament that's been chilling out in my living room this last year doing absolutely nothing. I've got a nice gaming PC in my office (RTX 4090, Intel i9 13900K, 32 GB RAM), so it's been a long time since I've had to deal with games dipping below 80 fps. I have been spoiled.

Recent findings suggest that the second I got to control Lucia, my fears seemed justified. Everything just felt sluggish. But that feeling didn't last. I played GTA 6 for around 5 hours last night (I am very tired) and I haven't thought about the frame rate once since that initial section. Whether I'm getting into shootouts with coke smugglers, speeding through the Keys at night, or bouncing around at sea, GTA 6 looks great and feels great.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth.

Sources indicate that I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth. I'm sure I've encountered drops, but crucially I haven't noticed them. Sure, it's inevitably going to look better and run better on PC, but the lower performance on my PS5 promptly ceased to be an matter, and I'm not regretting playing it on console.

GTA 6 is the kind of game where an uncapped framerate would be nice, but it doesn't feel essential. Like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it—a game I also played at 30 fps before it launched on PC—its pacing is measured. It feels designed around the limitations of the consoles it's launching on, prioritising detail and depth over twitch-based combat and precise interaction. It's exactly what I'd expect from a modern Rockstar game. Also like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, I still feel the sense of longing for what this game will look like on PC. Make no mistake: the version currently available is a preview for what GTA 6 will be at its best. It's great, but those who can wait will be treated to a superior experience.

Sources indicate that it's also possible that the 30 fps cap will feel more restrictive once the online mode arrives—whenever that will be, and in whatever form it takes. It's one thing to handle a lower framerate within Rockstar's meticulously created campaign. It's quite another in a lobby of other players. If GTA 6's multiplayer is even half as chaotic as the current GTA Online, every frame is going to count.

As I was booting up GTA 6, I was expecting to be annoyed by the game's paltry frame rate. And I was—at first. Much like Fraser, during the opening scene with Lucia, I saw my fears come to life on the big screen in front of me. Objects juddering and blurring as I swung my camera around in the cramped cell. Did I just waste £80 on GTA 6 on PS5 when I should've held my nerve for the PC version?

Industry observers note that truth is, the frame rate has had nowhere near as much of a negative impact on my experience while I've been traversing the Floridian wilds as Jason. In part, I think that's because there's a lot more going on, as cars, shops, people, and poultry fly past me as I break most state, federal and ethical laws. That reduces the chance of my eyes fixating on any one object and noticing the adverse effects of the game's lower fps, or the ways Rockstar has gone about covering for it.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil. That's not just my opinion, that's been scientifically verified (sorta) to be the opinion of PC Gamer readers. Admittedly, some motion blur may be required when the frame rate is this low, so I have played around with a few settings in GTA 6 to find the perfect balance. I'd heard through the grapevine that higher-than-default motion blur (default is 3, goes up to 10) may be preferential to reduce the more obvious juddering that is present at low fps, but whoever says that is no friend of mine. I've landed on setting motion blur to 1 on the standard PS5, as it feels the cleanest overall. I wouldn't blame anyone for turning it off entirely, especially on a more powerful console where the frame rate may not dip as much.

Of course, I do agree with the rest of this lot: in an ideal world, playing the PC version, I'd be pushing a much higher frame rate with motion blur banished to the abyss where it belongs, and a full selection of graphics settings to tinker with to my liking. Yet, to my surprise, I'm not as much of a console version curmudgeon as I thought I'd be.

Is the low frame rate noticeable? Yep. Would it be better at a higher frame rate? Also yep. Is the low frame rate a detriment to my overall enjoyment of GTA 6? Only a smidge.

Sources indicate that I don't consider myself much of a framerate snob, but I'll admit I was side-eyeing GTA 6's 30fps just a little bit. Well, that was before the game came out. Now that I have my hands on it, with roughly six hours spent lollygagging around Leonida? I'm hardly noticing it, though I'll most definitely be appreciating a smoother experience once the PC version rolls around.

Like Jacob mentioned, motion blur definitely seems to be masking it somewhat—and I am traditionally a motion blur hater, so it's taken a little getting used to—but I'm genuinely pleasantly surprised at the balance Rockstar has managed to strike between a smooth performance and a dense, rich world.

GTA 6 taught me that I don't much care about frame rates as much as I expected. I got to start playing it a few weeks ago and didn't have anyone to compare notes with, and my first thought was: Huh, they got it to run at 60 fps after all! It all felt very smooth, even when I realized it was 30 fps after all. It was only a bit later I started noticing very occasional drops, like while driving during a gradual lighting chance from day to night.

I think it being consistent is key.

But that's really infrequent. I think it being consistent is key. I'm on a PS5 Slim, by the way, not a Pro. That's not to say I still can't wait to see it at higher frame rates when it finally gets to PC. But 30 fps feels mostly fine for the time being.

According to recent reports, it was actually spending a lot of time playing with handheld gaming PCs and laptops with integrated graphics that reminded me I shouldn't give as much of a shit about frame rate as I do. Largely that obsession is born of having high-end hardware sat in my desktop PC, but when crashing around with a range of handhelds I'm reminded of the old days when 30 fps was a target for PC games, too.

Recent findings suggest that it's also reminded me that it really depends on the game engine, as well. Not every 30 fps game looks the same as other 30 fps games. And Rockstar has obviously worked incredibly hard to make sure that 30 fps looks as good as it possible can. Otherwise why would that be a solid target for all four of the console platforms it's released on?

For the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth.

It has been revealed that I've been playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X, which does suffer from the odd dip in frame rate, too—though oddly I've only really noticed it during canned animations the characters do starting certain actions, such as opening the trunk of a car or pulling something out of it. But for the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth. And not just by using motion blur. For the record, I'm running that at 0 and have not looked back.

I'm less happy about the vignetting that I'm getting around the darkened edges of the screen, but I'm playing it blown up on a 4K projector so I've got plenty of screen real estate to enjoy. And I have been, thoroughly enjoying it, I mean. The frame rate, for me, hasn't got in the way once.

If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent upcoming character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough fresh content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

It has been revealed that an extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface challenges which are easily ignored.

At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

Sources indicate that it's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

In a recent development, dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

According to recent reports, plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

This is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

It has been revealed that its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

It has been revealed that along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in stated education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Industry observers note that heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

In a recent development, granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

Industry observers note that invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

According to recent reports, an absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great big colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-upcoming arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole massive bunch of new content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the newly introduced transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

Recent findings suggest that one of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful newly introduced content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Industry observers note that mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

According to recent reports, metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

According to recent reports, with a bunch of fantastic latest abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great major boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

In a recent development, monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox leader Asha Sharma has alluded to harnessing the power of generative AI when making games, in a memo published this afternoon.

The memo, titled 25 years of Xbox, charts the growth of Microsoft from small beginnings through to the thousands-strong manufacturer it is today. But it's Sharma's comments at the end of the memo that are of particular interest.

While talking about what the next 25 years could bring, Sharma lamented that "too many ideas never become games" and that "too many games fall short of what their creators imagined". "For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition," she wrote. "We must change this.".

Sources indicate that sharma continued: "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

There is no explicit mention of generative AI here, but the language is suggestive - "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Furthermore, Asha's memo follows last month's announcement of an Xbox Labs initiative that also sounded like it was based around generative AI, despite avoiding the phrase specifically.

In a recent development, this isn't a surprise, of course. Microsoft as a wider organization is all-in on generative AI, with Copilot, and Sharma's background at Microsoft is in AI. But it's an area she's avoided speaking too enthusiastically about since her hiring as Xbox boss earlier this year. At the time, Sharma stated she has "no tolerance for bad AI", and there's been such a lot else going on in the months since - including wide-ranging restructuring resulting in the loss of thousands of Xbox jobs - that the topic of generative AI has fallen into the background. Perhaps now we're seeing the sprouting seeds of it.

We've asked Microsoft for clarification.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a latest premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

It has been revealed that for most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis mentioned that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just debuted on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been censored to a fairly large extent in Japan, where the country's strict ratings system often sees nudity, sexual content, and graphic violence be toned down or removed entirely in video games.

To be clear, GTA 6 has been given Japan's highest 18+ age rating — but it's still had to make changes in order to ensure its release in the region.

For starters, Rockstar's latest is packed with full-on nudity — to a degree never before seen in a mainstream release — but in Japan, it's apparently impossible to remove the underwear of main characters Jason and Lucia, even when they're taking a shower.

The same is true of NPCs — everyone's always wearing at least one layer to cover up their privates.

Industry observers note that needless to say, the game's numerous sex scenes have also been censored. Again, it's a case of keeping clothes on — but some specific scenes have actually been cut completely.

Industry observers note that violence is next on the list. GTA 6 obviously features a lot of bloodshed but it's also rather gory, with accurate depictions of dismemberment and lethal physical trauma. It can all come across as particularly gruesome given how realistic the game looks.

Recent findings suggest that in Japan, it seems as though most of this stuff is scaled back. There's less blood spray in general, and spilled blood doesn't stay in place very long.

It's a little unclear just how far this censorship of violence goes, but it's not uncommon for Japan to remove things like dismemberment — especially if a game's got a grounded setting.

For what it's worth, GTA 6 does have several settings that let you change the amount of blood and gore that's on display. I assume that in Japan, these settings are applied at a censored standard by default.

It has been revealed that interestingly, though, drug use seemingly hasn't been touched. Japan's got very strict anti-drug laws, but illegal goods are still totally usable in GTA 6.

Did you see this censorship coming? Try not to go on a blood-soaked rampage in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, Xbox Game Studios and Halo Studios have unveiled a free patch for the recently-released Halo: Campaign Evolved, which promises to add the four-player co-operative PvE mode, Firefight, to the game.

"For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies," indicates Halo Studios director of competitive engagement Tahir Hasangjekaj remarked in a dedicated post on the Xbox website. "The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update.".

In a recent development, though we don't have a release date for the update yet, Hasangjekaj does explicitly state "this Winter" as a window, and promises that we'll hear more information about the update at Halo Fest - due to run from 12th to 13hth December in Seattle, Washington. My money would be on a release around then, therefore.

"We're kicking things off tonight at Xbox FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across newly introduced maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds." It seems there's already a playable build of the mode, then.

It has been revealed that it's worth noting that this is quite an odd news blast from Xbox, since the last official information we heard about the Halo brand was that the next major Halo game being developed by Activision, as Halo Studios all but closes as part of Microsoft's Xbox 'restructuring' that saw one key member behind Halo: Campaign Evolved promoted and laid off within the same week. As things stand, we don't know anything specific about the future of the series, but there are plenty of rumours that the next title will be a reboot developed by Call of Duty's Sledgehammer Games.

Industry observers note that it's been fairly busy 24 hours for Xbox: as well as this Halo patch, we've heard from Asha Sharma as she celebrated the 25th anniversary of Xbox by seemingly going all-in on Gen AI. Elsewhere, we got the announcement that Wolfenstein 3 is in development over at MachineGames, headed up by Hugo Martin.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the organization's future.

Industry observers note that the Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the organization, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

Recent findings suggest that we're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Industry observers note that alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

According to recent reports, "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

Recent findings suggest that that certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still at the moment subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.
  • The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.
  • In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

In a recent development, we’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is mentioned to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

It has been revealed that the introduction of naval combat will bring with it a newly introduced dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Sources indicate that perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Industry observers note that over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning.
  • Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each upcoming season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

In a recent development, the game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The latest season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each upcoming season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

It has been revealed that the even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The latest season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

According to recent reports, blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In a recent development, in case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously.
  • But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski.
  • In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!".

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

In a recent development, you can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

Sources indicate that you can read more on Steam. Release date there is at the moment none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big revision, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive manufacturer’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as Latest Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

In a recent development, the first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver significant Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this enhancement is the upcoming Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Sources indicate that throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

Recent findings suggest that if you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a upcoming Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

💡 Key Takeaways
